At m=1 equality holds. This is the intended ordinary harmonic bound, not an alternative indexing or asymptotic estimate. This proof remains unfilled. Observed type: ∀ {m : ℕ}, 0 < m → ↑(harmonic m) ≤ 1 + Real.log ↑m Fresh v3 evidence preserves this exact type and unfilled statement artifact. Elaboration is evidence of the stated type, not of a completed proof.

With m,n positive, H_m<=1+log m and log(m/n)<=m/n-1 imply n*H_m<=n+n*log m<=m+n*log n<=2m. Thus the harmonic inequality follows directly from the actual largeSample definition n*log n<=m. For the integer conclusion, n=1 uses m>0; for n>1, log n>1-1/n gives n-1<n*log n<=m, hence n<=m since both are natural. No incorrect blanket assumption log n>=1 is used at n=1 or 2. This proof remains unfilled. Elaboration is evidence of the stated type, not of a completed proof.
